module_title: Mughal Empire - Foundation and Great Mughals
introduction: The Mughal Empire was established in 1526 after the defeat of the Delhi Sultanate in the First Battle of Panipat. It was one of the greatest and most expansive empires in Indian history. This level covers the chronology of the 'Great Mughals' and their major achievements.

core_concepts.title: Babur and the Foundation
core_concepts.description: Babur founded the Mughal dynasty in 1526 by defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat. He was the first to effectively use artillery/gunpowder in Indian warfare.

core_concepts.title: Humayun's Struggle and the Suri Interregnum
core_concepts.description: Humayun was defeated and exiled by the Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri (Battles of Chausa and Kannauj). However, Humayun recaptured the throne in 1555.

core_concepts.title: Akbar's Consolidation
core_concepts.description: Akbar (1556-1605) was the greatest Mughal emperor. He won the Second Battle of Panipat (1556) against Hemu, consolidated the empire through Rajput alliances, and introduced a syncretic code of conduct called 'Din-i-Ilahi'.

core_concepts.title: Jahangir and Shah Jahan
core_concepts.description: Jahangir's reign is considered the 'Golden Age of Painting', while Shah Jahan's reign is famous as the 'Golden Age of Architecture' (e.g., Taj Mahal, Red Fort).

core_concepts.title: Aurangzeb's Expansion and Decline
core_concepts.description: Aurangzeb achieved the maximum geographical expansion of the empire (reaching deep into South India). However, his orthodox religious policies and continuous wars drained the empire's resources, sparking its decline.

important_entities.name: Babur
important_entities.significance: Wrote his autobiography 'Tuzuk-i-Baburi' (Baburnama) and introduced the Charbagh (four-part garden) style.

important_entities.name: Sher Shah Suri
important_entities.significance: Ruled during Humayun's exile; introduced the silver 'Rupiya' and built the Grand Trunk (GT) Road.

important_entities.name: Akbar
important_entities.significance: The real consolidator of the empire; adopted a policy of religious tolerance known as 'Sulh-i-Kul' (universal peace).

important_entities.name: Aurangzeb
important_entities.significance: Ruled the empire at its territorial zenith, but his death in 1707 marked the beginning of the empire's rapid disintegration.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse the builders. The 'Agra Fort' was built by Akbar, whereas the 'Red Fort' in Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
Akbar's 'Din-i-Ilahi' was not a formal new religion, but rather an ethical code of conduct borrowing good points from various religions. Birbal was the only Hindu to accept it.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: B-Babur, H-Humayun, A-Akbar, J-Jahangir, S-Shah Jahan, A-Aurangzeb.

exam_strategy_tips: Always remember the years and combatants of the first two Battles of Panipat (1526 and 1556).
Direct 'Match the Following' questions regarding monuments and their respective builders are very common.
